# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 80 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 80 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_080_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Chapter 3

**1** He showed me many other trees, some budding and some withered. **2** And he said to me, "Do you see these trees?" "I see them, Lord," I said. "Those that are budding and sprouting," he said, "are those who are going to repent and live; for the Lord, seeing their repentance, thought good to grant life to them. **3** But those that are withered and not bearing fruit are those who have already apostatized in their hearts and will not return to repentance, nor will they return to the living." **4** I said to him, "Lord, why then did you bring some of the withered among those who repented?" He answered me, "So that, seeing the joyful appearance of those who are repenting, they might be put to shame and themselves repent; for if they see the glory of those who repented, and knew not the Lord before, but now know him, they will repent with all their hearts." **5** "But if they do not repent, Lord," I said, "what will happen?" "They shall die," he said, "those who do not repent at that point. But those who did repent and who lived righteously shall live with God. But those who did not repent and persisted in their wicked deeds shall die." **6** I said to him, "But those who returned the rod entirely green and cracked — who are they?" He said to me, "Always they were faithful and good, but they had jealousy toward one another over questions of pre-eminence and some glory. But they are all foolish, to have jealousy among themselves about preeminence." **7** "But those who returned their rods half-withered and cracked — who are these?" I said. **8** "These are those who were faithful but became rich and gained standing among the Gentiles. They put on great pride and became high-minded, and abandoned the truth and did not attach themselves to the righteous, but lived with the Gentiles, and this path seemed better to them. They did not depart from God, but remained in the faith, though they did not do the works of faith. **9** Many of them repented, but some remained in their deeds. These received their rods with the sap alive, for they did not depart from the living God, nor did the name from their lips. These therefore received their rods with sap."

---

*EMET preserves precise distinctions in the moral taxonomy: "apostatized in their hearts" (Greek apestēsan) vs. behavioral apostasy. "Pre-eminence" renders prōteia.*
